newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ gas/oil production up strongly in 1996 - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ gas/oil production up strongly in 1996 - SNZ.

text.p: Gas and oil production rose in the year to December, with gas production up 14 percent to 214.7 petajoules, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.
Annual gas production, while still below that achieved in 1992, has risen sharply over the past four quarters, with December quarter production up 11.7 percent over the same period in 1995.
Crude petroleum production in the quarter was unchanged from a year ago, but total production for the year was up 8.1 percent to 1.6 million tonnes.
Petroleum production is also lifting from a 1995 low, with production still well down on levels of about 1.9 million tonnes produced in 1991.
Bulk prices were generally firmer, with commercial natural gas prices up 0.5 percent on a year ago, LPG prices up 0.9 percent, petrol up 2.1 percent and diesel up 8 percent.
Statistics New Zealand said petrol and diesel refining was down for both the quarter and the year.

Petrol refining was down 13 percent for the quarter and 15 percent for the year to 1.3 million tonnes, due to a series of scheduled maintenance shutdowns. Diesel refining was down 17 percent for the quarter and 7.4 percent for the year to 1.4 million tonnes.
Electricity generation was down 1 percent in the quarter to 8198 gigawatt hours, with thermal generation up 48.7 percent and hydro down 9 percent.

Total production for the year was up 0.4 percent to 34.3 megawatt hours -- the highest December year production since records began in 1958. Compared with a year ago, commercial electricity prices were up 2.1 percent, while domestic prices were up 4.8 percent.
Coal sales continue their steady rise, with annual sales up 2.3 percent to 3.59 million tonnes, from about 2.5 million in 1989.
